cards.subtitle: Deterministic Enterprise Serverless ComfyUI & Multi-Tenant GPU Cluster scheduler evaluation (routing workflows by base-checkpoint SHA-256 affinity to warm GPU pools with 24GB/28GB DiT/UNet pinned in HBM, loading weights via zero-copy NVMe/shm mmap or GPUDirect Storage in <1.8s, and hot-swapping 150MB tenant LoRA adapters in <180ms so amortized GPU cost c_gpu(u) = c_0 / (1 + u) reaches 0.5000 at u = 1.0, locking C_active / C_warm = 1.0000x across all 17 cluster tiers u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive stateless round-robin dispatch and cold-start 28GB model downloading (which triggers VRAM eviction ping-pong and 120s cold-start stalls, inflating GPU spend by 1 + u to 1.2500x at T4, 1.5000x at T8, and 2.0000x at T16 across 16/17 tiers) and 64-worker VRAM cache quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Enterprise self-hosted ComfyUI / Diffusers Kubernetes clusters serving 500+ designers or multi-tenant SaaS APIs on H100 / L40S / A100 GPUs
Consistent-hash DAG routing that pins 24GB/28GB base models (Flux.1, Wan 2.2, SDXL) in dedicated GPU pools while hot-swapping 150MB tenant LoRAs in <180ms
Pre-staging `.safetensors` checkpoints on local NVMe RAID-0 / `/dev/shm` with zero-copy `mmap` and CRIU/CUDA snapshots (<1.8s warm-up)
not_for: Stateless round-robin load balancers (Nginx least_conn) that ignore which 28GB checkpoint is currently resident in each worker VRAM
Pulling 24GB weights over slow network NFS/S3 on every container scale-up
CPU-only static HTML web hosting with no GPU model weights
